claim: Malan (2021) surveys landscape-analysis applications and identifies automated algorithm configuration/selection as one of the main downstream uses, citing Kerschke et al. for a survey overview -- confirming algorithm/optimizer selection (not surrogate-model selection) is the dominant framing of ELA applications.
stance_target: ELA/landscape-analysis literature primarily targets optimizer selection
scope_conditions: survey of landscape analysis techniques and applications, evolutionary computation and optimization broadly
quoted_support: There are many attempts at automated algorithm selection using landscape features and the reader is referred to a survey by Kerschke et al. for an overview of studies.

claim: Yu, Tan, Sun, Zeng & Jin (IEEE CEC 2016) proposed an adaptive model-selection strategy for surrogate-assisted particle swarm optimization in which fitness landscape analysis is used to select among surrogate models -- a genuine precedent for landscape-driven surrogate-model selection, cited by Malan as reference [129].
stance_target: landscape-based surrogate-model selection exists in the literature, but as a narrow PSO/single-objective sub-area, not a GP-vs-neural-ensemble offline MBO framework
scope_conditions: surrogate-assisted particle swarm optimization (online, computationally-expensive single-objective optimization)
quoted_support: surrogate-assisted particle swarm optimisation, where fitness landscape analysis was used to select surrogate models [129]

claim: Werth, Pitzer & Affenzeller (EUROCAST 2019) performed a preliminary investigation into landscape analysis applied to surrogate (metamodel) functions rather than the true objective, and found the resulting landscape features were more indicative of the surrogate model's own architecture/bias than of the true underlying fitness landscape.
stance_target: landscape features computed on surrogate functions reliably characterize the true problem landscape
scope_conditions: simulation-based / computationally expensive optimization where surrogate models approximate the fitness function
quoted_support: Werth et al. performed a preliminary investigation into landscape analysis on surrogate functions and found that the landscape features were more indicative of the surrogate model than the original landscape.

claim: Malan explicitly flags landscape analysis of surrogate functions as an unresolved open research problem as of 2021, stating initial investigations were not very successful and further work is needed to find landscape techniques suitable for characterizing surrogate functions.
stance_target: landscape-driven surrogate-model selection is an immature/open problem, not an established practice
scope_conditions: surrogate modelling for computationally expensive optimization problems, as of 2021
quoted_support: Initial investigations into landscape analysis of surrogate functions were not very successful and further work is needed to identify landscape analysis techniques that are suitable for characterising surrogate functions so that the analysis is indicative of the characteristics of the actual landscape.

claim: Landscape analysis has also been applied to select CMA-ES algorithm configurations via a trained performance-prediction model based on landscape features, outperforming CMA-ES's default settings -- another example of landscape features driving optimizer/configuration choice, not surrogate choice.
stance_target: landscape analysis applications target optimizer configuration/selection
quoted_support: selection of CMA-ES algorithm configuration using a trained model for predicting performance based on landscape features that was shown to outperform the default setting of CMA-ES [128]

claim: Surrogate modelling is described as an important technique for managing computationally expensive optimization problems, but the survey's applications section (Section 4) otherwise catalogs landscape-driven selection uses across memetic-algorithm operator selection, CMA-ES configuration, and MOEA/D adaptive operator selection -- all optimizer/operator-level choices.
stance_target: scope of landscape-analysis applications catalogued in the survey
quoted_support: Surrogate modelling has become an important technique for managing optimisation problems that have computationally expensive objective functions.
